Investing.com -- Investing.com -- Mizuho has named Airbnb, Inc. (NASDAQ: ABNB) as its top pick across Internet coverage, raising its price target to $245 from $200 and maintaining an Outperform rating on the stock, which currently trades at $176.37.

The firm sees Airbnb positioned to build a multi-billion dollar hotel business on its platform while leveraging artificial intelligence to expand its dominance in the travel category beyond its legacy short-term rental and accommodation business. Mizuho notes that the company's significantly improved operating culture is increasingly showing up in results, with significant runway remaining for both the company and its shares.

The analyst firm increased its estimates above consensus, projecting room night growth of approximately 12% in 2027 and 11.5% in 2028. Revenue growth is expected at 15.4% in 2027 and 14.8% in 2028, with earnings per share growth of 18% and 29%, respectively.

Mizuho forecasts adjusted EBITDA of $6.16 billion in 2027, compared to the Street estimate of $5.77 billion, and $7.38 billion in 2028 versus Street estimates of $6.57 billion.

The firm expects EPS of $6.43 in 2027 and $8.26 in 2028, compared to consensus estimates of $6.23 and $7.35. The bullish case centers on Airbnb's improving operating culture driving faster execution and accelerating growth in the core business, marking the fastest room night growth in three years.

Mizuho highlighted upcoming product cycles including hotel supply expansion, dynamic pricing, advertising, loyalty programs, and AI expansion into new verticals. The firm noted that hotel growth accelerated from the second quarter to the third quarter, contributing an estimated 70 basis points of growth.

The price target of $245 is based on 30 times 2028 estimated GAAP EPS and 25 times enterprise value to EBITDA. The stock currently trades at approximately 29 times 2027 estimates and 23 times 2028 estimates.

ABNB Q3 2026 deep dive: AI-driven product expansion accelerates growth and margin gains

Online accommodations platform Airbnb (NASDAQ:ABNB) beat Wall Street's revenue expectations in Q3 2026, with sales up 18.9% year on year to $4.87 billion. Its non-GAAP profit of $3.16 per share was 10.7% above analysts' consensus estimates.

Is now the time to buy ABNB? Find out in our full research report (it's free).

Airbnb (ABNB) Q3 2026 highlights:

Revenue $4.87 billion vs S&P analysts' estimates of $4.75 billion (18.9% year-on-year growth, 2.6% beat)

Adjusted EPS $3.16 vs S&P analysts' estimates of $2.85 (10.7% beat)

Adjusted EBITDA $2.51 billion vs analyst estimates of $2.36 billion (51.5% margin, 6.1% beat)

Operating margin 41.5%, up from 39.7% in the same quarter last year

Nights and experiences booked 155 million, up 21 million year on year

Market capitalization $100.3 billion

StockStory's take

Airbnb's third quarter results were well received by the market, with a strong positive reaction driven by revenue and profit exceeding Wall Street expectations. Management attributed the quarter's outperformance to accelerated growth across all major regions, the successful rollout of new features, and an expanding product portfolio. CEO Brian Chesky cited years of foundational investment in technology and organizational structure as key enablers, emphasizing, "This did not happen overnight... we spent years changing how Airbnb operates, and now we are seeing the results."

Looking ahead, Airbnb's management is focused on leveraging advancements in artificial intelligence, the continued expansion of hotel and service offerings, and new partnerships to fuel further growth. CFO Ellie Mertz highlighted ongoing investment in growth initiatives while maintaining profitability, noting that "the prioritization around continuing this momentum continues to be the top priority." The company is also preparing to launch travel-focused AI agents and deepen integration with partners to capture a larger share of the travel market.

Key insights from management's remarks

Management credited the quarter's performance to robust guest demand, expanded offerings, and operational efficiencies enabled by AI, which collectively accelerated growth beyond analyst expectations.

AI-powered efficiency gains: Airbnb's adoption of artificial intelligence has accelerated product development, enabling the launch of over 50 new features in the quarter—nearly 70% more than the previous year. AI initiatives have also reduced customer support costs by resolving 40% of issues without human agents and contributed to margin expansion.

International and demographic expansion: All five of Airbnb's core markets delivered double-digit growth in nights booked, with standout performance in Brazil (up over 30%) and India (up over 60%). Gen Z emerged as the fastest-growing guest segment, highlighting success in attracting younger travelers.

Hotel and services growth: The company's hotel pilot, now expanded to over 60 destinations, is growing at a markedly faster rate than the core business. Hotels are attracting new users—35% of guests whose first booking is a hotel return to book a home within a year. New services like car rentals, meal delivery, and local gear offerings are also gaining traction.

Dynamic pricing and product innovation: Dynamic pricing tools, supported by AI, are being adopted by hosts to optimize occupancy and revenue, with early results suggesting the potential to lower guest prices and increase host earnings. The rollout of the single service fee and guest travel insurance has enhanced marketplace transparency and monetization.

Leadership and partnership initiatives: The hiring of Pepijn Rijvers as Chief Business Officer is expected to strengthen international expansion and performance marketing, especially in the growing hotel segment. Strategic partnerships, such as the exclusive deal with American Express Travel, are broadening Airbnb's reach, especially among luxury travelers.

Drivers of future performance

Airbnb's outlook centers on sustained product innovation, AI-driven operational leverage, and expansion into new travel services and partnerships.

AI agent rollout and integration: Management plans to launch custom travel-focused AI agents in the first half of next year, aiming to streamline trip planning and booking. These agents will increasingly integrate with external partners, enabling users to book a broader range of travel services directly within Airbnb's platform. The company believes this will differentiate Airbnb from general-purpose AI tools by offering tailored, visual interfaces for travel.

Hotel, services, and loyalty expansion: Hotels are expected to remain a major growth lever, with management projecting multi-billion-dollar revenue potential in coming years. New service offerings—including car rentals and meal delivery—are being integrated natively, while a loyalty program is under consideration to increase user retention and engagement as more verticals are added.

Pricing optimization and marketplace competitiveness: The ongoing adoption of AI-powered dynamic pricing and fee simplification is designed to balance affordability for guests with earnings optimization for hosts. Management sees these initiatives as critical for maintaining competitive prices, attracting Gen Z, and expanding in both established and emerging markets.

Catalysts in upcoming quarters

Looking forward, the StockStory analyst team will closely monitor (1) the rollout and user adoption of AI-powered travel agents, (2) the pace of hotel and new services expansion, and (3) the impact of strategic partnerships like American Express Travel on customer acquisition and revenue mix. The effectiveness of dynamic pricing tools and the development of a loyalty program will also be important indicators of Airbnb's ability to sustain momentum.

title: Airbnb's growth spurt comes with a catch
detail:
Airbnb's growth spurt comes with a catch
Tobi Opeyemi Amure, Celine Provini
Sun, November 8, 2026 at 9:07 AM CST 4 min read
ABNB
Trade Airbnb on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Booking a vacation rental used to mean paying up front.

You found the place, entered your card and hoped your plans held. If they didn't, you were stuck chasing a refund.

Airbnb (ABNB) changed that math this year, and travelers noticed. Revenue rose 19% to $4.9 billion in the third quarter, its fastest growth in three years, according to Skift.

CEO Brian Chesky has called pricing "a massive lever" for growth, Rental Scale-Up reported.

However, a subtle shift has emerged in how Airbnb is earning that growth.

According to a Deutsche Bank research report seen by TheStreet, a meaningful slice of Airbnb's acceleration came from its Reserve Now, Pay Later program, even as the core business also sped up.

Airbnb's pay-later bookings did a lot of the lifting

The numbers were strong across the board.

Nights and seats booked rose 16% to 155 million, up from 10% growth in the second quarter, Rental Scale-Up reported. Gross booking value climbed 21% to $27.7 billion.

Deutsche Bank analyst Benjamin Black broke down where that growth came from in a Nov. 6 note titled "Growth is Back in the Neighborhood."

Related: KeyBanc says consider buying shares of popular travel giant now

"RNPL [Reserve Now, Pay Later] provided 3ppt of net nights growth in 3Q, versus approximately 1.5ppt in 2Q, but the underlying business also accelerated," wrote Black.

By my math, pay-later bookings accounted for nearly a fifth of Airbnb's 16% growth. Without them, nights would have grown about 13%.

Hotels added less than a point, Black wrote. That suggests "core homes growth reached approximately 12%," he added.

Black kept his Buy rating and raised his price target to $220 from $200. The stock closed at $170.13 on Nov. 5, the note showed. By my math, that target implies about 29% upside.

Airbnb bookings jumped 16% as pay-later gained traction, despite cancellations rising to 19% and Deutsche Bank seeing upside.Jose A. Bernat Bacete / Getty Images
More travelers are canceling

Pay-later bookings come with a trade-off.

Airbnb's cancellation rate rose to about 19% from about 16% a year earlier, Rental Scale-Up reported. The company's filings say pay-later bookings cancel more often than bookings paid up front.

CFO Ellie Mertz called that rate "very healthy in the travel space," the outlet reported.

More on Airbnb:

American Express adds $250 Airbnb credit, but there's a catch

Airbnb just found an unexpected way to make AI pay

Airbnb quietly makes big change customers need to know about

Guests on the program aren't charged until eight days before their free-cancellation deadline. On Airbnb's strictest Firm policy, that's about 38 days before check-in.

If you book this way, I'd put that charge date in your calendar. Your card gets hit weeks before the trip, and missing the cancellation window can cost you the full stay.

Airbnb Inc. (ABNB) delivered strong Q3 revenue and free cash flow (FCF) on Nov. 5, with higher FCF margins. ABNB stock soared over 11% on Friday. Is it too late to get in? This article covers some ABNB plays.

ABNB was up $20 in midday trading on Friday, Nov. 6, at $189.99. That's up from $164.39 on Oct. 30, and a recent low of $149.58 on Sept. 23. But can it move significantly higher?

ABNB stock - last 6 months - Barchart - Friday, Nov. 6, 2026

Analysts think so. The average price target (PT) from 44 analysts surveyed by Yahoo! Finance is $200.40. And Barchart's mean survey PT is $199.84, both higher than Friday's close.

Let's analyze why

Strong FCF and Revenue Forecasts

Airbnb said its gross booking value rose 21% YoY in Q3 and revenue grew 19%. Moreover, Q3 free cash flow (FCF) gained 32.8% to $1.4 billion with a 29% FCF margin (29% last year).

Moreover, its trailing 12-month (TTM) FCF rose 20.4% to $4.9 billion, representing 35% of revenue (38% last year). These figures are on page 14 of its shareholder letter.

ABNB FCF and FCF margins - page 14 of Q3 shareholder letter

This implies that as Airbnb's revenue rises, the company's strong FCF margins could keep pushing FCF even higher.

For example, analysts expect revenue to rise 7.75% from $14.18 billion in 2026 to $15.28 billion in 2027.

So, for example, if the company maintains a 35% to 38% FCF margin performance (say 36.5%), FCF could exceed $5.5 billion:

$15.28b x 0.365 = $5.5772 billion FCF

That's +13.7% above the Q3 TTM FCF of $4.904 billion (see above). In other words, its valuation should rise. But by how much?

Fair Market Value for ABNB Stock

Over the last 5 years, Seeking Alpha says the average price/cash flow multiple has been over 24.2 times (i.e., a 4.1% FCF yield). So, ABNB could be worth $140 billion in the next year:

$5.5772 / 0.041 = $140.78 billion fair market value (FMV)

That is over $27.4 billion above its present $113.375 billion market cap, according to Yahoo! Finance. In other words, its PT is 24.2% higher:

$189.99 x 1.242 = $236 PT

However, this assumes revenue will rise 7.75% next year, and its average FCF margin will be 36.5%. If figures come in lower than this, ABNB won't be worth 24% more.

And, as always, there is no guarantee the stock will rise to exactly its underlying value. It could underperform or overshoot.

Airbnb: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
The Motley Fool Team, The Motley Fool

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 5, 2026, Airbnb (NASDAQ:ABNB) announced revenue of $4.9 billion and expanding night volumes across all core markets. For long-term investors, the key issue is whether structural efficiency gains and platform expansions can support lasting profit growth. Three things management said stand out.

1. Boutique Hotel Listings Drive Traffic and Funnel Guests to Core Homes

Adding hotels expands options for short stays without diluting platform identity. Hotel listings bring first-time users into the ecosystem, and a substantial portion eventually books residential properties.

In fact, approximately 35% of guests whose first booking is a hotel, they come back and they book a home within a year.
-- Brian Chesky, Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer

2. Automated Support Tools Lower Unit Costs While Expanding Margins

Deploying artificial intelligence software to resolve routine guest inquiries improves operational efficiency without expanding headcount. Lower support expenses preserve capital while supporting higher profitability as total booking volumes increase.

What this means is that customer support cost per booking has declined more than 17% year-over-year, driven in large part by improvements to our AI assistant.
-- Brian Chesky, Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer

3. Share Buyback Expansion Capitalizes on Robust Free Cash Flow Generation

Substantial cash generation allows management to return capital directly to shareholders. Expanding share repurchases signals balance sheet confidence while reducing total share count over time.

Finally, during Q3, we repurchased $700 million of our common stock, enabled by our strong balance sheet and significant cash flow generation, leaving $2.7 billion remaining under our existing authorization. And today, we're pleased to announce Board approval of a new $12 billion share repurchase program on top of this existing authorization.
-- Ellie Mertz, Chief Financial Officer

Looking Ahead

Accelerating booking volume across international markets reflects operational momentum, giving leadership space to expand secondary services. Management relies on proprietary listing density, direct host communication, and flexible payment arrangements to maintain marketplace liquidity. Executives prioritize overall booking momentum and full-year margin expansion.

Airbnb is back in growth mode. It's rare for a marketplace of our size to reaccelerate growth, but that's exactly what we're doing. Q3 was our fastest revenue growth in more than 3 years.

A blowout quarter with a lot to like

Airbnb's revenue grew 19% year-over-year, or 16% excluding any currency effects, which was significantly higher than analysts were expecting. On the bottom line, earnings per share were $3.16, compared to the $2.85 expectation among Wall Street analysts.

Demand was extremely strong as well. Nights and seats booked through the platform reached 155 million, up 16% from a year ago, and gross booking value grew 21% to $27.7 billion. Plus, the company remains an absolute cash machine. Airbnb has generated $4.9 billion in free cash flow over the past 12 months, and adjusted EBITDA increased by 22%.

The company is also starting to explore new growth areas and gain traction in some. Airbnb recently began adding adjacent services such as meal delivery and car rentals, and traditional hotels now account for a significant (but still single-digit) share of booked nights. These are all small pieces of Airbnb's revenue today, but they provide Airbnb with credible pathways to maintaining an elevated growth rate.

Looking ahead, management expects Airbnb's fourth-quarter revenue to fall in the range of $3.22-$3.28 billion, representing 17% growth at the midpoint.

Putting its cash to work

Airbnb has over $12 billion in cash on its balance sheet and, as mentioned, is generating free cash flow of roughly $5 billion annually. Well, the board authorized a new $12 billion share repurchase program, and that's on top of the $2.7 billion left under the existing authorization. Even after Friday's pop, the new buyback alone represents more than 10% of Airbnb's market value.

It's worth noting that Airbnb uses these buybacks (in part) to offset dilution from stock-based compensation, and the share count has shrunk and should continue to do so.

Interested in Airbnb, Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

Airbnb held up better than the broader technology market during the Nov. 5 sell-off before jumping following its earnings report.

Third-quarter revenue rose 19%, bookings accelerated, and management raised its full-year outlook.

A new $12 billion share repurchase authorization adds to the positive outlook, although valuation and slowing benefits from flexible payments remain considerations.

Thursday, Nov. 5, was one of the market's roughest sessions in years. The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52%, its worst day since April 2025, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq-100 dropped 6.36%, its steepest decline since March 2020. Selling was driven in part by fears that Democrats' midterm gains could slow the AI data center buildout, and chip stocks took the brunt, with the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ: SMH) falling by roughly 11%.

Airbnb (NASDAQ: ABNB) didn't escape entirely, slipping 3.5% to close at $170.13. But it held up far better than the broader tech market, and it was still up about 3.5% on the week and more than 25% year to date heading into its report. That relative strength made Airbnb's third-quarter earnings release even more interesting. Would the results justify the stock's outperformance and notable relative strength, or give investors a reason to lock in gains?

→ Duolingo's User Growth Is Outpacing Bookings, But Is Its Strategy Paying Off?

At least initially, the answer was clear. Shares jumped about 11% in after-hours trading to trade near $189, within roughly 2% of their 52-week high of $193.45.

Airbnb's Revenue and Booking Growth Accelerate

Airbnb's third-quarter revenue rose 19% to $4.87 billion, its fastest growth in more than three years and well ahead of the roughly $4.75 billion analysts expected. Earnings of $3.16 per share also beat the $2.85 consensus by 31 cents, though a lower tax provision flattered the year-over-year comparison.

→ 3 Dividend ETFs Offer Different Ways to Navigate the Post-Election Sell-Off

The demand metrics were arguably more impressive. Gross booking value climbed 21% to $27.7 billion, while nights and seats booked rose 16% to 155 million, a sharp acceleration from 10% growth in the second quarter. About three percentage points of that came from the expansion of Airbnb's Reserve Now, Pay Later option. Even excluding that lift, nights booked grew about 13%, which still marked an acceleration from the prior quarter.

The strength was also broad-based. Every region posted double-digit growth in nights booked, North America grew at its fastest pace in four years, and nights booked through Airbnb's app rose 29% to account for 66% of the total.
